title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Discover ten distinct study environments across the Case Western Reserve University campus, from historic reading rooms to modern innovation centers.

cards.title: Quiet Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Kelvin Smith Library, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Enter the second floor for a strictly silent environment. This space is designed for deep focus and individual work without the distraction of group discussions.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated silent study space located on the second floor of the main campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: Kelvin Smith Library provides a Quiet Reading Room specifically intended for quiet study.
cards.source_title: Spaces | Kelvin Smith Library - Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; CWRU ID required for late-night access.

cards.title: Main Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Corner of Euclid Ave. and Adelbert Rd.
cards.notes: Study among historic portraits and chandeliers in this Classical Revival space. It offers a traditional academic atmosphere with large windows facing Euclid Avenue.
cards.short_summary: A historic, high-ceilinged reading room known for its quiet, traditional academic ambiance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Allen Memorial Medical Library features a main reading room and three large quiet study rooms.
cards.source_title: About Us | Cleveland Health Sciences Library | Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Accessible via CWRU ID card; typically open 10:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays.

cards.title: Floor 6 Co-working Space
cards.subtitle: Richey Mixon Building
cards.notes: Utilize the open co-working area on the sixth floor for brainstorming and group projects. No reservation is required for the general open seating areas.
cards.short_summary: An open-access innovation and co-working floor within the seven-story makerspace.
cards.evidence_claim: Floor 6 of Sears think[box] features open co-working space available for use without prior reservation.
cards.source_title: Meeting Spaces | Sears think[box] - Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; check website for specific daily hours (typically 9 a.m. - 7 p.m. weekdays).

cards.title: Weatherhead Student Center
cards.subtitle: 11119 Bellflower Road
cards.notes: Find cloistered desks and secluded study spots on the upper levels of this Frank Gehry-designed building. It offers a modern, quiet alternative to the main floor lounge.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level study area located above the main entrance of the business school.
cards.evidence_claim: The Peter B. Lewis Building student center includes comfy chairs and a quieter upper area with cloistered desks.
cards.source_title: Best study spots on CWRU's campus - The Observer
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours; study rooms can be reserved by students.

cards.title: Tinkham Veale Booths
cards.subtitle: 11038 Bellflower Road
cards.notes: Use the spacious booths for a mix of social study and snack access. These spots are ideal for students who prefer a comfortable din over absolute silence.
cards.short_summary: Spacious seating booths located in the central campus hub near dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tinkham Veale University Center offers booths that are spacious and located near food options like Med-23.
cards.source_title: A letter to those interested in new study spots - The Observer
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for students with CWRU ID; public access during daytime hours.

cards.title: Upstairs Study Area
cards.subtitle: 11440 Murray Hill Road
cards.notes: Head to the renovated upstairs seating for a quieter environment away from the main dining floor. Some rooms in this area include whiteboards for group work.
cards.short_summary: A renovated seating and study area located on the upper level of the South Side dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Fribley Commons has renovated seating upstairs that is far enough from noise for quiet work and includes whiteboards.
cards.source_title: Best study spots on CWRU's campus - The Observer
cards.access_notes: Accessible during dining hall operating hours.

cards.title: Harris Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: 11235 Bellflower Road
cards.notes: Visit this specialized library for a quiet, focused environment. It is part of the Mandel School and offers a smaller, more intimate setting than KSL.
cards.short_summary: A quiet academic library serving the Jack, Joseph and Morton Mandel School of Applied Social Sciences.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lillian and Milford Harris Library provides study spaces and is part of the Spartan Reservation System.
cards.source_title: Lillian and Milford Harris Library | Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9 a.m. – 5 p.m.; closed on weekends.

cards.title: HEC Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: 9501 Euclid Avenue
cards.notes: Explore various study areas throughout the pavilion, including Student Learning Communities on the fourth floor with kitchenettes and lounge seating.
cards.short_summary: Modern study and collaboration spaces located within the Health Education Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Samson Pavilion offers a variety of study spaces, including Student Learning Communities on the fourth floor.
cards.source_title: Dining and Study Spaces | Health Education Campus | Case Western Reserve University
cards.access_notes: Priority access for health profession students; CWRU ID required for entry.

cards.title: Tomlinson Quiet Lounge
cards.subtitle: Case Quad
cards.notes: Find a cozy spot in the swivel chairs on the second floor. This area is known for being quiet and convenient for students with classes on the Case Quad.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, comfortable lounge area located on the second floor of Tomlinson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor of Tomlinson Hall is described as cozy and quiet, fitted with swivel chairs.
cards.source_title: A letter to those interested in new study spots - The Observer

cards.title: Nord Basement Lounge
cards.subtitle: 10900 Euclid Avenue
cards.notes: Relax on the sofas in the Nord Hall basement for reading or laptop work. It provides a more casual, low-light environment compared to the upper floors.
cards.short_summary: A casual lounge area with sofas located in the basement of Nord Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nord Hall basement has cozy sofas suitable for laptop work or reading.
cards.source_title: A letter to those interested in new study spots - The Observer
